papers.title_en: Ultra-compact twin stars with hybrid equations of state from bosonic dark matter
papers.authors: Ishfaq Ahmad Rather, Sarah Louisa Pitz, Jürgen Schaffner-Bielich
papers.evidence: 致密星混合状态方程与孪生星结构，关联中子星状态方程
papers.tldr: 致密星内部夸克物质相变与暗物质共存时，其质量-半径稳定性会显著改变。数值研究发现，自相互作用玻色子暗物质能够移除强子-夸克混合分支间的不稳定段，使孪生星序列连续化，并产生两类超致密天体：暗物质晕类（占比>0.9）和暗物质核类（占比<0.02），可通过正常物质表面红移区分。该结果可为未来X射线和引力波观测探测暗物质及夸克相变提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: The properties of compact stars with a strong first-order phase transition to quark matter and with an additional fluid of self-interacting bosonic dark matter (DM) are studied. We find that the inclusion of DM changes considerably the stability of mass-radius configurations relative to the naive one-fluid criterion. For compact star configurations with similar masses and different radii, so-called twin stars, the presence of DM removes the unstable segment between the hadronic and the hybrid branch, so that the stable mass-radius sequence becomes continuous after the onset of the phase transition to quark matter. We furthermore find stable ultra-compact objects (UCOs), defined by a total compactness $C = M_\text{tot}/R_\text{grav} \ge 1/3$. We observe two distinct classes of UCOs: a DM-halo class with $f_\text{DM} \gtrsim 0.9$, and a DM-core class at $f_\text{DM} \lesssim 0.02$. The two classes can be separated by the surface redshift of the normal matter, which reaches $z=0.73$--$0.77$ for the DM-core class and stays below $0.45$ for the DM-halo class. Finally, we find hybrid star solutions of 'ultimate twins' with similar mass and visible radius, but different dark matter content, leading to different tidal deformabilities and surface redshifts. Future X-ray and gravitational measurements of ultra-compact neutron stars with radii and masses outside the allowed neutron star range can thereby probe the presence and the properties of DM in addition to a first-order phase transition to quark matter.

papers.title_en: A fast, wide-field, and real-time imaging prototype for large aperture arrays
papers.authors: Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, Jishnu Thekkeppattu, David Humphrey
papers.evidence: 面向快速射电暴毫秒级实时探测定位的成像原型
papers.tldr: 实时探测快速射电暴等瞬变源需要毫秒级成像，传统相关器O(N^2)复杂度难以满足大规模阵列需求。提出基于FPGA的EPIC直接成像方案，以O(N log N)计算复杂度避免显式互相关，利用并行FFT流水线实现高效处理。初步结果显示其计算效率优于GPU且功耗更低，并具备良好可扩展性。该原型为SKA-Low等下一代宽视场望远镜提供了可行的实时成像路径。
papers.abstract_en: Real-time processing on sub-millisecond timescales is essential for detecting fast astrophysical transients such as fast radio bursts (FRBs) and prompt electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational-wave mergers. Immediate localisation enables rapid multi-wavelength follow-up and maximises scientific return. As a result, real-time capability has become a key requirement for modern wide-field aperture arrays, which are increasingly being deployed at scales of thousands to tens of thousands of antenna elements. However, traditional correlator architectures scale as $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$, creating significant computational, bandwidth, and power challenges for large-$N$ arrays. These constraints often limit field of view, angular resolution, or observing duty cycle, ultimately reducing transient discovery potential.   Direct imaging of the full field of view using E-field Parallel Imaging ``Correlator'' (EPIC) offers a promising alternative by avoiding the explicit formation of pairwise correlations. EPIC can achieve $\mathcal{O}(N \log N)$ computational scaling for dense aperture arrays and has been demonstrated on the Long Wavelength Array (LWA) station in Sevilleta (USA) using Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). However, GPU implementations can be limited by memory bandwidth in low-bitwidth gridding and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) workloads. We, therefore, are developing a prototype implementation of EPIC using Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) that exploits highly parallel FFT pipelines to improve computational efficiency and reduce power consumption. Using preliminary results, we evaluate its performance particularly from the viewpoint of scalability, and discuss its suitability for next-generation instruments including SKA-Low and mid-frequency aperture arrays.
